Baltimore road closures

Roads closed or slowed by flood water and blocked by fallen trees at each time step (T1–T5). Inferred from free public data, not observed closures.

Road key

Closed: water ≥ 1 ft (≈ 0.3 m, no safe driving speed) Crawl: 0.5–1 ft water (≈ km/h) Slowed: 0–0.5 ft water (≈ km/h) Blocked by fallen trees (one sampled outcome) Low-lying, not connected to the bay (may pond)
■ 1–5%■ 5–20% ■ 20–50%■ >50%

Fallen-tree model

How closures are inferred

Flood. Roads are cut into ~50 m pieces and sampled every 8 m against NOAA inundation at each 0.5 ft from 0 to 10 ft. A piece's depth at water level L ≈ L − (lowest level that reaches it). Speed follows Pregnolato et al. (2017), v(w) = 0.0009w² − 0.5529w + 86.9448 km/h for depth w in mm, ≈ 0 at 300 mm, so ≥ 1 ft is closed. Pieces already under water at 0 ft are treated as bridges/tunnels and left open.

Fallen trees. Illustrative, not calibrated. Trees near a piece = (trees per 100 m) × canopy % × length, with canopy from NLCD 2021 around the road. Each tree fails with lognormal probability Φ(ln(gust/median)/0.3), and a failed tree blocks the road with probability 2% (Interstate), 15% (US/MD route) or 40% (local street). Trees stay down for the rest of the storm, so blockage uses the highest gust so far.

Not modeled: pluvial (rain) flooding, waves, debris other than trees, power lines, closures ordered by agencies, clearing crews.

Sources

Roads: MD iMAP road centerlines (MDOT SHA): Interstates, US and MD routes, named public local roads. Alleys and private roads are excluded.

Flood: NOAA OCM sea-level-rise inundation, a static "bathtub" model with hydro-connectivity, not a surge forecast.

Canopy: NLCD 2021 tree canopy cover (USFS). Speed–depth: Pregnolato et al. 2017, Transp. Res. D 55:67–81.

Isabel imagery: NASA GIBS MODIS. Basemap: Esri World Imagery. Hospitals: OpenStreetMap via Overpass.
